studies.question: Which LLM gets the cheapest positive reply?
studies.headline: Gemini 3.1 Pro wins at $214 per positive reply.

charts.title: Cost per positive reply (USD, lower is better)
Gemini 3.1 Pro: cost per positive reply by month

conclusion: Gemini 3.1 Pro: 37 positive replies · 98,982 emails, $7,902 spent.
Over time: $103 in Apr, $563 in Sep.

studies.question: Which LLM gets the most positive replies?
studies.headline: Gemini 3.1 Pro leads with 3.7 positive replies per 10,000 emails.

charts.title: Positive replies per 10,000 emails (higher is better)
Gemini 3.1 Pro: positive replies per 10,000 emails by month

conclusion: Gemini 3.1 Pro: 37 positive replies · 98,982 emails.
Over time: 3.2 /10k in Apr, 2.1 /10k in Sep.
Only a LLM past 1,000 emails can lead; a smaller one is drawn and marked thin.

charts.title: Cost per positive reply if the sequence stopped here (USD, lower is better)
Each email on its own: cost per positive reply (USD, lower is better)

studies.question: How many follow-ups get the most positive replies?
studies.headline: Positive replies keep coming through 2 follow-ups: the last one adds 1.4 per 10,000 people.

result.unit: positive replies per 10,000 people, all follow-ups

charts.title: Positive replies per 10,000 people, adding each follow-up (higher is better)

conclusion: Counted per person reached, so a follow-up is judged on what it adds, not on how many emails it took.
+ 1 follow-up: +2.5 /10k.
+ 2 follow-ups: +1.4 /10k.
+ 3 follow-ups: +0 /10k.

studies.question: Should we track opens for the cheapest positive reply?
studies.headline: No clear winner: 0.12% with tracking off, 0.10% with it on (p 0.56, not significant).

charts.title: People who replied positively (%, higher is better)

conclusion: An email costs the same with or without the pixel, so the cheaper positive reply is the arm with more of them per person.
Tracking was on from 2026-02-10 to 2026-06-28 and off until 2026-09-12: two periods, not a split test, over 49,834 people.

studies.question: Should we track opens for the best reply rate?
studies.headline: Tracking off wins: 0.39% of people replied, against 0.29% (p 0.04).

charts.title: People who replied, any reply (%, higher is better)
Bounced (%, lower is better)

conclusion: Auto-replies and out-of-office messages are not counted as replies.
Tracking was on from 2026-02-10 to 2026-06-28 and off until 2026-09-12: two periods, not a split test, over 49,834 people.
